cards.claim: Increasing the momentum coefficient increases the timescale required for the accumulation to adapt to loss landscape changes, which impedes training
cards.conditions: SGD with momentum, CIFAR-10 Wide ResNet, variable momentum coefficients
cards.effect: Accuracy drops from 94.5% to 93.3% when momentum increased from 0.9 to 0.98 with batch size scaling
cards.evidence: Experimental comparison across training schedules with matched epoch counts
cards.quote: Furthermore, when we increase the momentum coefficient we increase the timescale required for the accumulation to forget old gradients (this timescale is also 1/(1-β)). Once this timescale becomes several epochs long, the accumulation cannot adapt to changes in the loss landscape, impeding training.

cards.claim: Initialization bias correction for large batch sizes causes instabilities during early training stages
cards.conditions: Large batch training with momentum, early warmup phase
cards.evidence: Empirical observation from large batch experiments
cards.quote: However when the batch size is large, we found that this often causes instabilities during the early stages of training.

cards.claim: Ghost batch norm ensures mean gradient is independent of batch size
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10 Wide ResNet 16-4, ghost batch size 128, physical batch size 128-6400
cards.effect: Maintains gradient statistics consistency across batch size changes
cards.evidence: Experimental design choice validated by equivalence of learning curves across batch sizes
cards.quote: We use ghost batch norm ( Hoffer et al., 2017 ) , with a ghost batch size of 128. This ensures the mean gradient is independent of batch size, as required by the analysis of Smith & Le (2017) .

cards.claim: Increasing initial learning rate and batch size together reduces parameter updates needed while maintaining accuracy
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10 Wide ResNet, initial lr 0.5 vs 0.1, initial batch 640 vs 128, momentum 0.9
cards.effect: Reduces parameter updates from 29000 to under 6500 while maintaining 94.5% accuracy (vs 94.4% baseline)
cards.evidence: Experimental results across five runs per schedule
cards.quote: "Increased initial learning rate" requires under 6500 updates, reaching a final accuracy of 94.5 %. Across five additional training runs for each schedule, the median accuracies were 94.3 %, 94.2 %, 94.2 and 93.5 % respectively.

cards.claim: Accumulation variable grows toward steady state over approximately 1/(1-β) epochs timescale, suppressing initial parameter update magnitude
cards.conditions: SGD with momentum coefficient β, initialization of accumulation at zero
cards.effect: Slowed convergence at training start proportional to 1/(1-β), requiring additional epochs
cards.quote: This variable tracks the exponentially decaying average of gradient estimates, but initially it is initialized to zero. We find that the accumulation grows in exponentially towards its steady state value over a "timescale" of approximately 1/(1-β) training epochs. During this time, the magnitude of the parameter updates is suppressed, reducing the rate of convergence. Consequently when training at high momentum one must introduce additional epochs to allow the dynamics to catch up.

cards.claim: Batch size increase reduces parameter updates while maintaining learning curves per epoch when combined with noise scale preservation
cards.conditions: CIFAR-10 Wide ResNet, three equivalent noise scale decay schedules: constant lr/decay bs, hybrid, increasing bs/constant lr
cards.effect: Same test accuracy per epoch (94.3% across conditions) but parameter updates reduced from 80k to 29k via batch increase alone
cards.evidence: Direct comparison of training and test curves across three schedules
cards.quote: The three training curves are almost identical, despite showing marked drops as we pass through the first two steps (where the noise scale is reduced). These results suggest that it is the noise scale which is relevant, not the learning rate.

cards.claim: Maximum batch size constraint improves stability of distributed large-batch training beyond theoretical limits
cards.conditions: Inception-ResNet-V2 on ImageNet, momentum scaling experiments, distributed training
cards.effect: Training stability improvement, enables reaching 2500 parameter updates vs larger accuracy variance without cap
cards.evidence: Experimental design choice with observed variance reduction
cards.quote: We introduce a maximum batch size, B_max = N. This ensures σ² ≥ η, and it also improved the stability of our distributed training.

cards.claim: Increasing momentum coefficient beyond 0.9 without sufficient epoch extension degrades final accuracy despite reducing parameter count
cards.conditions: ImageNet Inception-ResNet-V2, momentum 0.9 vs 0.975, both at 90 epochs, batch size scaling with momentum
cards.effect: Accuracy drops from 78.8% (momentum 0.9, 6000 updates) to 76.8% (momentum 0.975, 2500 updates)
cards.evidence: Experimental comparison with 1-2 runs per schedule
cards.quote: Finally "Momentum 0.975" achieves final accuracies of 77.5 and 76.8 in under 2500 updates.
